note: A dated note, not a maintained news service. Review when policy status changes.

groups.heading: Announced by the government, not yet law
groups.meaning: Set out in a government announcement. It becomes law only if Parliament passes it.

entries.text: The triple lock stays as it is until April 2030. From then the government plans a rule of inflation or 2.5%, whichever is higher, and more if that is needed to keep pace with earnings.
The government says it will legislate for the change during this Parliament. In our reading the rule needs a change in the law, because in some years it would pay less than the rise in earnings.
A National Care Service, with free personal care for older people, is planned for the next Parliament. It would not cover bed and board.
The government says the savings from the pension change will be used for the care service, and that the service will not be paid for by borrowing.
The government gives estimates of the saving for the end of the 2030s and for 2050. It has not published how they were made.

groups.heading: In law, and earlier commitments
groups.meaning: Set out in law, in a government document or in a published commitment.

entries.text: The full rates for 2026/27 rose on 6 April 2026, in line with earnings growth.
The law requires an increase at least in line with earnings.
In England, a commission on adult social care is due to report in summer 2027.
The Pensions Commission plans its final report for spring 2027. Its terms of reference do not mention the triple lock by name.

groups.heading: What research bodies say
groups.meaning: Findings and views of named bodies. None is government policy.

entries.text: The Institute for Fiscal Studies says the change removes the permanent ratchet, and that the savings will be small at first. Its deputy director says they should not be expected to pay for universal social care in the next Parliament. The government has announced free personal care, in phases, not universal care.
The Resolution Foundation welcomed the change.

groups.heading: Reported, not confirmed
groups.meaning: News reports. They are evidence of what was reported, not of a decision.

entries.text: PA News reported that the care service is for England. A minister was reported as saying that a share of the money would go to Wales.

groups.heading: What other parties said
groups.meaning: Statements made on 29 September 2026. Reform UK's is from its own page. The others are from news reports.

entries.text: Reform UK says it will keep the triple lock.
The Conservative leader, the Liberal Democrat leader and the First Minister of Scotland criticised the change.

groups.heading: What we did not find
groups.meaning: A search that finds nothing is not proof that nothing exists.

entries.text: We found no Bill, no technical note and no costing method for the change.
The announcement does not say which nations the care service covers, or how pensioners in the other nations would be treated.
We found no published analysis of who would gain and who would lose.
We found no costed proposal to means-test the State Pension.
